description: Enclosed research facility inside the ISS Destiny module, providing a 255-liter sealed work volume with two levels of containment via negative pressure, HEPA/charcoal/catalyst air filtration, power (+28V DC, +12V DC, -12V DC, +120V DC), and gaseous nitrogen supply. Houses the BASS flow duct, a black anodized rectangular wind tunnel (7.6 cm x 7.6 cm x 17 cm) with an upstream fan, flow restrictors, honeycomb flow straightener, and inlet screen.
limitations: Maximum oxygen concentration capped at 21% by volume; cannot test elevated-oxygen/reduced-pressure Exploration Atmospheres.
name: Microgravity Science Glovebox
purpose: Provides a sealed, controlled work volume aboard the ISS for microgravity combustion experiments such as BASS, BASS-II and BASS-M.

description: Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR), part of the Fluids and Combustion Facility (FCF) aboard the ISS. Houses the Multi-user Droplet Combustion Apparatus (MDCA) and the ACME spherical flame experiments.
name: Combustion Integrated Rack
purpose: Provides a controlled microgravity combustion research facility aboard the ISS for droplet combustion and gaseous flame experiments such as FLEX and ACME CFI-G.

data_quality.notes: Converted from the verified PSI-69 page on 2026-11-13. The PSI-69 page spells the name with a typo (Appartatus); the correct spelling is used here. Verify against the cited NASA source before marking confirmed.

description: Multi-user Droplet Combustion Apparatus (MDCA), the droplet combustion apparatus inside the Combustion Integrated Rack. Used for the FLEX droplet flame extinguishment tests.
name: Multi-user Droplet Combustion Apparatus
purpose: Ignites and observes relatively large liquid fuel droplets in microgravity to determine flammability limits and suppressant effectiveness.

description: Spacecraft Fire Experiment (SAFFIRE) module: a large-scale flame-spread experiment flown in the Cygnus pressurized cargo module after it deberthed from the ISS. A sample card sits in the middle of a large flow duct, with air drawn through by fans and flow straighteners. Two cameras capture flame images; thermocouples, radiometers, solid-state sensors and anemometers record temperatures, radiation, gas composition and flow velocity.
name: Spacecraft Fire Experiment module
purpose: Studies how rapidly a large-scale fire grows in low gravity and the low-g flammability limits of spacecraft materials, in an expendable vehicle with no risk to crew.
supported_measurements: Pressure, CO2 and O2 mole fraction

description: Comparative Soot Diagnostic Hardware: the smoke diagnostic hardware used by SAME and SAME-R in the Glovebox, with a near-field hardware section and a Far Field Box attached to the Glovebox. SAME-R reused the SAME on-orbit hardware, with the M-pass instrument replacing one Commercial Diagnostic Enclosure.
name: Comparative Soot Diagnostic Hardware
purpose: Generates smoke from overheated spacecraft materials under controlled conditions and measures smoke particulate size distribution and smoke-detector response in microgravity.
